title: Temporal Fourier Optics Reveals Hidden Hybridized Light-Matter States
authors: Juan-Feng Zhu, Wenjie Zhou, Shihao Feng, Zicheng Song, Ruicong Zhang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Rengming Liu, Lin Wu
abstract: Spectral measurements provide fundamental insights into wave systems by revealing resonances, mode hybridization, and light-matter interactions. However, intrinsic dissipation and measurement-induced spectral broadening often conceal the underlying hybridized light-matter states that give rise to measured spectra. Here, we establish a space-time Fourier correspondence that interprets spectral broadening as an effective temporal attenuation, giving rise to a temporal Fourier optics framework for recovering hidden spectral information. Implemented through a temporal point-spread-function (TPSF) reconstruction method, the framework compensates the effective temporal decay before Fourier transformation, directly reconstructing intrinsic spectral responses from experimentally measured spectra without repeated frequency synthesis or model-dependent fitting. We experimentally validate the approach in deterministic single-molecule Au nanosphere dimers and open Au@Ag nanorod- and nanotriangle-based plasmonic nanocavities coupled to J-aggregate excitons. Across these diverse platforms, TPSF consistently reconstructs hidden upper and lower polaritonic branches, thereby revealing the underlying hybridized light-matter states and strong coupling that remain unresolved in conventional scattering spectra. The reconstructed spectra agree closely with the recently developed complex-frequency formalism while offering a considerably simpler and more experimentally accessible implementation. Beyond strong light-matter coupling, temporal Fourier optics establishes a general framework for uncovering physical states hidden by dissipation, opening new opportunities for spectroscopy, imaging, sensing, and inverse wave measurements across photonics and wave physics.
summary: The authors introduce Temporal Fourier Optics (TFO) to overcome the challenge of spectral broadening caused by dissipation in optical measurements. By treating this broadening as a compensable temporal attenuation, they develop a TPSF reconstruction method. This technique successfully reveals hidden hybridized light-matter states in plasmonic and molecular systems, offering a general tool for spectroscopy across various wave physics domains.
main_problem: Intrinsic dissipation and measurement-induced spectral broadening obscure underlying hybridized light–matter states, making their direct observation challenging in spectroscopy.
main_result: The Temporal Fourier Optics (TFO) framework successfully reconstructs these hidden upper and lower polaritonic branches across diverse platforms, revealing strong coupling regimes otherwise unresolved by conventional methods.
method: A temporal point-spread-function (TPSF) reconstruction method is implemented, which compensates for effective temporal decay before performing a Fourier transformation to recover intrinsic spectral responses.
model_or_system: The work applies the framework to deterministic single-molecule Au nanosphere dimers and open Au@Ag plasmonic nanocavities coupled to J-aggregate excitons. The underlying physics is governed by wave propagation principles analogous to spatial diffraction.
key_observables: Reconstructed upper and lower polaritonic branches, intrinsic spectral responses, scattering cross sections.
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime ($	ext{g} > (\gamma_{	ext{cav}} - \gamma_e)/4$), temporal decay rate ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: Spectral broadening is mathematically equivalent to an effective temporal attenuation that can be inverted via the TFO framework.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical foundation by drawing an analogy between spatial PSF (diffraction) and temporal TPSF (dissipation). It then details the mathematical framework for compensation, followed by experimental validation across multiple plasmonic and molecular systems to demonstrate hidden state recovery.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, experimentally accessible tool—TFO—to probe fundamental quantum phenomena like strong light-matter coupling in dissipative environments, extending beyond standard complex-frequency formalisms.
